answer: Each Ember Cartographer agent carries a cryptographic quill that timestamps every reputation event and links it to a verifiable age ledger stored on the reef of distributed nodes. As the tide of activity flows, reputation points accrue proportionally to continuous task completion and decay when the agent goes silent, forcing any new identity to start at zero. An attacker must therefore purchase enough computational stake to simulate years of continuous work, making a Sybil attack cost comparable to the economic value of the targeted services.
